Three things worth knowing before you write the client:

* **Always
send `Idempotency-Key` on a launch.** It spends model credits, so a\n retry of a dropped response must not run the goal twice. Re
playing a key\n returns the original run with `deduped: true` and starts no second runner\n and consumes no quota. Omitting the
header is read as a request that declined\n to identify itself, and gets a fresh run every time.\n* **Check `canceled` before rep
orting a failure.** A stopped run carries\n `status: \"failed\"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than\n a s
tatus of its own. `stale: true` is the third case: the runner went silent\n and the watchdog settled the run.\n* **`targetId`, no
t `hostId`, identifies a target.** Two environments can\n resolve to the same host with different servers, so a run can hold two\

n targets that share a `hostId`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Launching **spends**: a run fans out into `targets × iterations`
> sessio
ns. Two different `429`s can come back; the per-minute burst brake\n> (retry in seconds) and your plan's daily launch cap (resets

at UTC midnight).
> Both normally carry `Retry-After`; back off on your own when one does not.

**Swarms, insights**: what a ru
n revealed. Read these in order of cost: the\nroll-up and the scorecard are deterministic and free, the findings registry\naggrega

tes them, and swarm run insights run a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals-overview` | Project roll
-up: recent runs, goal-completion rates, repeat failures, trend |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/scorecard` | One run's determinist
ic rubric result. No model, no spend |\n| `GET .../goal-findings` | Criteria that keep failing, tracked across swarm runs |\n| `PO
ST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Hide a finding |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Un-hide it |\n| `
GET .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Poll a swarm run's generated insights. **404 = nobody asked** |\n| `POST .../swarm-run
s/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Request them. `202`; scheduled, not done |\n| `DELETE .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Cancel a

generation still `pending` |

Two arithmetic traps worth naming, because both produce numbers that look
plausible and are wrong

:

* **Divide by `sessionsGraded`, never by the session total.** Three failures
 out of four graded sessions, in a run that at

tempted forty, is 75%, not
 7.5%.
* **`failedGradingCount` is not `failCount`.** A crashed judge is not a
 regression, and fo

lding the two together makes one look like the other.

And one modelling note: a finding's `status` is a lifecycle:
`new | recu
rring | regressed | resolved`. `dismissed` is *not* one of them.\nDismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a finding can be b

oth recurring
and dismissed, and hiding one never claims it stopped happening.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting swarm run insight
s consumes **no credits**; the model cost is on\n> MCPJam. It still counts against the `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts\n> RE
QUESTS and is **shared** with eval-run and user-testing insights, so a\n> request here takes one from there too. Poll the `GET` ra

ther than
> re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice.
>
> Three refusals, three different meanings: a sho
rt `429` is the per-minute\n> brake (wait seconds), a `429` naming `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger\n> (its `Retry-After`, whe
n present, counts to UTC midnight), and a `403` means\n> the feature is not available to your organization; waiting will never hel

p.

**User testing** (`/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/study`,
`.../studies/...`): publishing an environment
for real visitors, reading what\nthey did, and controlling who can reach it. A **study** is a published\nenvironment: one per env

ironment, addressed by its own id once it exists.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `PUT .../environments/{environmentI
d}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent: republishing returns the existing study, and `created: false` says so. Project **admin** |\n|
`DELETE .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Unpublish.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted: false` when there
was nothing published |\n| `PATCH .../studies/{studyId}` | Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/
sessions` | What visitors did: one row per session, with feedback and a first-message preview |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sess
ions/{sessionId}` | One session's transcript, paged. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/guest-exe
cution` | The spend dial for anonymous visitors: daily credits, computer starts, concurrency |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rota
te-link` | **Mint a new share link.** No body; the new secret is minted server-side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/members` | Inv
ite someone (or change their role) on an `invited_only` study |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{memberIdOrEmail}` | Remo
ve someone. Their grant is revoked, ending their live sessions |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point the study at a dif

ferent environment in the same project |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who already used it.** It
stops the\n> old URL from granting NEW access; the grants already redeemed under it stay\n> valid. That is the single most import
ant thing to know here, because rotation\n> is what you reach for when a link leaks, and on its own it does not undo the\n> leak.
Rotate *and* remove the members you did not intend to have.\n>\n> What DOES take effect at once, ending live sessions rather than
waiting for\n> expiry: unpublishing, tightening `mode`, and removing a member. Those bump\n> the study's `accessVersion`, and a se
ssion minted under an older version\n> stops working. None of them reverse by calling the opposite; a re-invited\n> member gets a

new session, not their old one.
>
> Read `accessVersion` off the publish and rebind responses. The update and
> rotate response

s do not carry it.

**User testing, what visitors did**: the analytics reads, and the model pass
over them. Read these in cost

order: metrics, usage and signals are
deterministic and free; the insights request runs a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/metrics` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` splits r
eal visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the sessions used. **Check `
scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in the current window, and
where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, dismissed ones inc
luded |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/windows/{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, which is
not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `202` wit
h the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the window has not been mined yet |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release a gene
ration stuck `pending`. Takes `windowId` in the body |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismiss a fi
nding. Keyed on its stable id, so it stays dismissed when insights regenerate |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId
iled`, `skipped`, and `deferred` describe session\ncoverage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete work;\n`a
